name: Oklahoma
summary: OSCN (oscn.net), the official free host of the statutes, constitution, court-rule appendices, case law with public-domain citations (2019 OK 12, ¶ 10) and dockets, now refuses all automated access by robots.txt 'Disallow: /' (earlier the same day a Cloudflare Turnstile wall), so every OSCN row is blocked; the Legislature's statute files are robots-disallowed and rules.ok.gov (OAC, Oklahoma Register) answers robots.txt with a bot check. Working routes: Justia 2025 statutes, constitution and year-listed opinions of all three appellate courts (WebFetch; tier 2), the Senate's constitution PDFs (script, tier 1, Jan 2022) and Cornell LII for the OAC (script). Supreme Court Rules, ORPC, District Court Rules, OCCA Rules, the Register and certiorari dispositions have no unblocked free source. Justia's 2025 page for a section amended by several 2025 acts is a text-less version list: fall back to the linked 2024 edition and disclose it.

citation_map.notes: Oklahoma style: '12 O.S.2021 § 2012(B)(6)' (edition year glued to O.S.), '12 O.S. Supp. 2024 § 3226'; Bluebook 'Okla. Stat. tit. 12, § 95'; West 'Okl.St.Ann.'. Statute sections may be dotted (701.7) or hyphenated (63 O.S. § 1-705, 10A O.S. § 1-1-105): a single § keeps hyphens; after §§ only the first number is taken, so '§§ 2001-2027' reads as 2001. Civil procedure and evidence are statutes (Pleading Code 12 O.S. §§ 2001-2027, Evidence Code §§ 2101-3009), routed by the 'Pleading Code / Evidence Code' pattern as well. Court rules are cited as statute appendices ('Rule 1.36, Oklahoma Supreme Court Rules, 12 O.S. Supp. 2021, ch. 15, app. 1'; ORPC 5 O.S. ch. 1, app. 3-A; RGDP app. 1-A; OCCA Rules 22 O.S. ch. 18, app.); bare 'Rule 1.36' is context_required. Public-domain citations: 'YYYY OK N' (Supreme Court), 'YYYY OK CIV APP N', 'YYYY OK CR N', 'YYYY OK AG N' (AG opinions), pinpoint by ¶; mandatory since 1997 and assigned retroactively on OSCN (from memory). COCA neutral-citation year is the publication year and may follow the decision year. Bare P.2d/P.3d cites, bare dockets (OCCA F-/C-/S-/RE-/PC-YYYY-N, Supreme Court 'No. 121,610', SCBD-N) and 'cert. denied' are context_required. OAC colon form '165:10-3-1' is distinctive only with 'OAC'/'Okla. Admin. Code'; the bare form is context_required (New Jersey N.J.A.C. also uses a colon). The earlier clash with Ohio's bare 'OAC …' pattern was fixed in oh.json (now context_required). CourtListener ids from memory, unverified. Trailing-marker rule cites ('Rule 1.191, Okla. Sup. Ct. R.') and prose '§ 701.7 of Title 21 of the Oklahoma Statutes' are covered (independent regex tests 2026-10-17).
